entities.name: The Final Call
entities.notes: Nation of Islam newspaper, Chicago-based. Online Edition began 1995 per institutional history.

entities.name: Nation of Islam
entities.notes: Chicago-headquartered religious-political movement; publisher of The Final Call.

entities.name: Chicago Defender
entities.notes: Flagship Black newspaper of Chicago; website launched December 2004, podcast 2005.

entities.name: Real Times Media
entities.notes: Parent company of the Chicago Defender at the time of the 2004 site launch; CEO Clarence Nixon quoted in trade press.

entities.name: Obama for Illinois (2004 Senate campaign)
entities.notes: Barack Obama's Illinois U.S. Senate campaign; site v1 dated early 2003 by enthusiast retrospective (CONJECTURAL).

entities.name: AfroLink Software
entities.notes: Early African American BBS founded 1990 by Kamal Al-Mansour. National context; no Chicago tie shown.

entities.name: AfroNet
entities.notes: FidoNet-based network founded 1993 by Ken Onwere, serving Africans and African Americans across North America. National context; no Chicago tie shown.

entities.name: U.S. National Telecommunications and Information Administration (NTIA)
entities.notes: Primary government source: Falling Through the Net series, racial access/infrastructure figures.

entities.name: Data & Society
entities.notes: Research institute; hosted McIlwain's Black Software Databites talk (video selection).

entities.name: Ward Christensen
entities.notes: Chicago; co-created the first dial-up BBS (CBBS, 1978) with Randy Suess. Prehistory context.

entities.name: Randy Suess
entities.notes: Chicago; co-created the first dial-up BBS (CBBS, 1978) with Ward Christensen. Prehistory context.

entities.name: Kamal Al-Mansour
entities.notes: Founded AfroLink Software (1990). National context.

entities.name: Ken Onwere
entities.notes: Founded AfroNet (1993). National context.

entities.name: Clarence Nixon
entities.notes: Real Times CEO; quoted in 2005 trade press on the Defender's December 2004 website launch.

entities.name: Roland S. Martin
entities.notes: Journalist whose 2004 arrival at the Chicago Defender preceded its website launch; per retrospective the paper had no site before him.

entities.name: Charlton D. McIlwain
entities.notes: NYU scholar; author of Black Software (2019), the secondary scholarship documenting AfroLink/AfroNet. Documents adopters; not a primary participant.

entities.name: Jason Scott
entities.notes: Computer historian (textfiles.com); director of BBS: The Documentary (2005), CC-licensed archival record of BBS culture.

entities.name: Nicholas Rougeux
entities.notes: Web designer; author of the 'Obama's online evolution' Wayback-based retrospective (CONJECTURAL source).

entities.name: Unnamed NOI college students
entities.notes: Built The Final Call's Online Edition as a promotional tool for the 1995 Million Man March. Digital intermediaries; identities unrecovered.

entities.name: Unnamed Black Chicago BBS operators, listserv moderators, church webmasters, bloggers (1990-2005)
entities.notes: Asserted only as a category of missing actors; no individuals recovered. Central gap of this brief.

note_on_role_tags: Inventor/engineer tags are reserved for creators of technology (Christensen, Suess). Adopter tags apply to those who took up existing technology (institutions, unnamed operators). Entrepreneur/operator apply to founders of Black digital systems. Cultural transformer is used once (Roland S. Martin) for an actor whose arrival reshaped an institution's media practice. Charlton D. McIlwain and Nicholas Rougeux are tagged scholar/documentarian rather than adopter/innovator: they document the history, they are not primary participants in it.
